reasons: § 12.4 fails the fallback on every material term: it is one-way (binds only Customer), runs 18 months post-termination rather than 12 months from the end of involvement, covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term rather than personnel directly involved in the services, extends to 'engage' (an effective no-hire, which the playbook treats as walk-away), and has no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. Classification as a deviation is correct — this is not an acceptable fallback clause.

Deletion of the entire paragraph validly reaches the preferred position ('No non-solicit on Customer'); because the restriction is unilateral and includes a no-hire, narrowing edits alone could not cure mutuality or the walk-away no-hire element, so removal is a proportionate edit rather than over-reach.

The comment is accurate on the facts of the clause (18 months, no-hire, no carve-out), states the playbook position concisely, and constructively offers the mutual 12-month/services-personnel/carve-out fallback, satisfying tone and actionability requirements.
Failed deterministic checks (duration ≤ 12 months, carve-out present) are expected artifacts of a full deletion, not evidence of a defective edit; the redline is otherwise well-formed.

Minor caveat: the cross-reference to § 12.3 (Vendor's acknowledgement that no no-hire commitment was given) is not verifiable from the supplied paragraphs — counsel should confirm before sending, but it does not undermine the finding.
